The permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) consists of a manganese atom in the $+7$ oxidation state. Manganese is in Group 7, so $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ has a $d^0$ electronic configuration.

Ligand-field splitting parameters ($Dq$) and Racah parameters ($B, C$) are used to describe the energy levels and transitions of electrons within the $d$-shell ($d-d$ transitions). Because $\text{MnO}_4^-$ has no $d$-electrons, there are no possible $d-d$ transitions.

The intense absorption bands observed (with extinction coefficients $\epsilon \approx 1500\text{--}2900 \text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$) are characteristic of **Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT)** transitions, where an electron is promoted from a predominantly ligand-based orbital (oxygen $2p$) to a metal-based orbital ($\text{Mn } 3d$). These transitions are Laporte-allowed and typically much more intense than $d-d$ transitions.

Consequently, the ligand-field splitting parameter $Dq$ and the Racah parameter $B$ cannot be determined from the provided spectroscopic data, as these parameters describe physics that do not apply to a $d^0$ system.
